summary: One medium admission bypass in the integrated M3 request-control middleware: non-API routes perform authentication outside all new rate limits. No supported issue found in the reviewed JSON-reader byte/concurrency/cancellation bounds, bounded rate-bucket state, health exemptions, operator configuration validation, or fixed aggregate diagnostics. Reviewed root baseline 2f82c735859a10dc1d378ae702d5931b0cda6275 plus integrated working-tree sources; exact SHA-256 pins are in request-boundary-reviewed-hashes.json. This report records the pre-correction state; lead owns the announced fix and revalidation.
coverage: Read effective AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, declared startup project context, workflow/review guidance, adversarial-review contract, bounded review brief, M3.6 implementation brief and applicable inventory/phase requirements. No source edits or delegation performed.

Inspected apps/server/src/request-controls.ts in full: byte count and Content-Length validation, bounded buffer growth, invalid UTF-8/JSON, simultaneous-reader admission, abort/timeout races, cancellation that never settles, continuously ready chunks, reader locks/listeners/timers, bounded token-bucket cardinality and expiry, trusted direct-peer/fallback identity, fixed path categories, health exclusions and closed lifecycle.

Inspected apps/server/src/diagnostics.ts in full and new call sites: allowlisted counters/gauges/histograms, bounded numeric values, copied snapshot payloads, aggregate periodic output, category labels without paths, principals, goals, content or credentials, and absence of a diagnostic HTTP route.

Traced apps/server/src/app.ts middleware and shared JSON-body helper plus apps/server/src/auth/http.ts authentication, sign-in/CSRF/capability boundary and JSON-body helper. Searched server request-body consumers to confirm authentication and general JSON routes use readJsonBody; existing multipart evidence parser remains separately byte/concurrency bounded.

Inspected apps/server/src/server.ts configuration load before storage/listening, shutdown signal and diagnostics cleanup. Inspected installed @hono/node-server/dist/index.mjs request wrapper and unread-body cleanup: default auto-cleanup drains at most 500 ms/64 MiB before closing socket; no unbounded-drain finding raised.

Read apps/server/test/request-controls.test.ts and diagnostics.test.ts, including declared/actual multibyte size checks, malformed JSON, nonsettling cancellation, abort/timeout release, tiny chunks, token refill/cardinality, forwarded-header spoofing, principal quotas, health availability, lifecycle, configuration and fixed-label privacy coverage. These tests were inspected, not executed by this reviewer.

Executed one no-port native Node reproduction against actual createApp/createService/AuthService with explicitly in-memory SQLite and VISUA_DATABASE_URL/VISUA_TEST_DATABASE_URL/VISUA_DB removed. With peerPerMinute=1: three /api/meta invalid-token requests returned [401,429,429] and performed one credential lookup; eight /assets/synthetic.js requests returned eight 401s and performed eight further lookups. Diagnostics counted only the three API requests. Process exited 0 and memory store was closed.

Verified all seven primary source/test SHA-256 pins were unchanged at review completion, before the lead-announced app.ts correction. Added auth/service.ts, evidence-http.ts and the installed Node adapter digest to the source-pin artifact.

findings.mechanism: beforeAuth and afterAuth apply only to /api/*, while authenticate(auth) applies to every path. An unauthenticated caller sends Authorization: Bearer vsa_synthetic_invalid_token on /assets/anything or arbitrary SPA paths. authenticate invokes resolveApiToken before the static/404 response; resolveApiToken performs an indexed database lookup for each vsa_-prefixed token. These requests bypass peer/principal admission and request diagnostics entirely, even after exhausting the same peer API bucket. Arbitrary session cookies similarly invoke resolveSession and its database lookup. This leaves authentication work outside the intended request boundary and permits unthrottled database work on public non-API paths.
findings.evidence: Executed reproduction using actual createApp, createService({database: :memory:}), AuthService(loadAuthConfig({})), Diagnostics and loadRequestControlConfig({}) overridden with peerPerMinute:1. Wrapped auth.resolveApiToken to count invocations while delegating to the real method. API result: statuses [401,429,429], credential calls 1. Same app/direct-peer fallback then requested /assets/synthetic.js eight times: statuses [401,401,401,401,401,401,401,401], credential calls 8. request counters contained only other.4xx=3. auth/http.ts:82-97 runs credential resolution on all non-health paths; auth/service.ts:391-408 and 451-457 confirm database work. Counterevidence: API routes are correctly limited before authentication, health/ready skip authentication, and missing credentials avoid lookups; none prevents an attacker explicitly providing a synthetic vsa_-prefixed credential on an arbitrary non-API path. Lead independently confirmed mismatch and announced correction; that new state is outside these recorded source pins.
findings.recommendation: Restrict authenticate(auth) to the protected /api/* scope, since static assets and SPA shells do not need identity, or apply admission to every path that resolves credentials. Add a focused regression proving no token/session lookup occurs on non-API paths and exhausted API peers cannot trigger further credential resolution. Revalidate the corrected middleware ordering before deployment.

limitations: This is one bounded source review and isolated in-memory reproduction, not capacity measurement or a network/load test. No live services, ports, PostgreSQL, browser, Docker, Git operations or external providers were used.
Full test/typecheck/integration gates are owned and running by the lead and were deliberately not duplicated. Tests read here establish checked-in coverage only.
The report is bound to pre-correction hashes. Lead has announced the app.ts authentication-scope fix and a regression; their resulting source/test state must be checked separately.

Rate quotas were reviewed as deliberately per-instance. Distributed quotas, wider existing application error logs, SSE authorization internals, and complete multipart-parser redesign are outside this bounded assignment.
